title: Biomarker and digital monitoring for prevention of disease progression of rheumatoid arthritis
summary: This study aims to record the progression of rheumatoid arthritis in the usual routine with the goals of detecting an increase in disease activity at an early stage and preventing progression. Clinical examinations, laboratory parameters and various questionnaires are used to collect data on physical function, quality of life and psychological well-being on a quarterly basis. Using an activity tracker, health parameters are recorded over 7 consecutive days to measure physical activity and general condition. Immunological markers are used to record immune activation in comparison to other rheumatic diseases. The examinations for rheumatoid arthritis take place once a quarter over a period of one year.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Age >18 years, m/f/d
- For patients diagnosed with RA or for control participants (rheumatic disease, but no RA or symptomatic for diagnostic clarification without evidence of rheumatic disease)
- Consent to participate in the study and the resulting data collection and processing
- Ability to understand the patient information and willingness to sign the informed consent form
Exclusion criteria:
- Psychiatric illness that restricts understanding of the study protocol (unable to give informed consent)
- Taking antibiotics at the start of the study
